text:
Cutter Gauthier is the reason people outside Anaheim are watching the Ducks. He has 18 points in his last 10 games against 11.4 our numbers expected from his chances, and the trade that sent him west keeps coming back: this week Flyers general manager Daniel Briere pushed back on an Elliotte Friedman report about the deal, saying Friedman was "Just trying to get some free clicks on it" (as quoted by Sportskeeda). Sportsnet's Eric Engels wondered aloud whether Gauthier's contract might end up looking cheap.

The top line, with captain Mikael Granlund (16 points in 10) and Beckett Sennecke (16 in 10), has outscored opponents 7-5 at 5-on-5. It has done that with only 43% of the expected goals (the quality of the chances) in those minutes. That is finishing carrying the process, and finishing tends to cool.

The bigger worry is behind them. Ville Husso (.825) and Lukas Dostal (.838) have both had rough last five starts, and Anaheim has allowed about 11 more goals than its chances against would predict. Laurent Brossoit went back to San Diego anyway, after a 4-1 start.

At 11-12-1 with 49% of the expected goals, the record is roughly honest. The Ducks are winless in three, outscored 15-8, and our playoff odds have them at 44%. What we'd watch: whether the saves show up before the top line comes back to earth.
